prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in League City, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported wrist fracture. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1033; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officer narrative, League City, Texas. At approximately the time of the call, I responded to a rear-end collision on the roadway involving two vehicles. Driver 1 was stopped in the travel lane when the front of Driver 2's vehicle struck the rear of Driver 1's vehicle. Driver 2 told me the impact occurred exactly as Driver 1 described it. Two independent witnesses on the scene gave matching accounts, and the photographs I took show the rear-end damage that is consistent with the reported impact. The damage is largely in line with the force of a collision of this kind. Driver 1 reported a wrist injury and said the impact threw them against the steering wheel. That injury is consistent with the mechanism of this crash. Passenger was in the front seat and was confirmed present by Driver 1, Driver 2, and both witnesses. Nothing observed or reported by anyone at the scene suggests prior damage to Driver 1's vehicle. Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the policy covering that vehicle, as shown on the proof of insurance presented at the scene.
